title: BMW Agents -- A Framework For Task Automation Through Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary:
The paper addresses the limited industrial use of standalone LLMs, which lack access to confidential, proprietary business data, and the drawbacks of fine-tuning on company data. It proposes an enterprise agent engineering framework that automates complex processes through multi-agent collaboration across mixed modern and legacy IT systems. A Planner Agent decomposes a user request into tasks on a Task Queue. Narrowly scoped agents are coordinated by a conversational strategy, ConvPlanReAct, in which a Semantic Matcher selects the best agent for each task and a Mention Matcher handles explicit message passing. In the software development example, a Coder (File I/O tool), Architect (Web Search tool), and Tester (Code Execution tool) iterate as an Agent Unit, and a Verifier Agent checks the final output against the original request. Other mechanisms include tool-list refinement with implicit schemas, episodic memory, human feedback, and pause-and-resume of workflows.

The excerpt reports no quantitative results. The software development workflow appears only as a qualitative illustration (Figure 16), with no metrics on output quality, task success, or efficiency.
